sentences.text: Alxasaurus possessed an abbreviated tail, shortened metatarsals, broad feet, and long, recurved hand claws similar to derived therizinosaurs. Its tail was short compared to other theropods, and it had an abbreviated metatarsus, a trait convergent with basal sauropodomorphs.

The tooth-bearing part of the Alxasaurus dentary measured 18.5 cm in length. Although poorly preserved, evidence suggests Alxasaurus had interdental plates. Alxasaurus had a beak on its small head and about forty tiny teeth at the back of its mouth.

Alxasaurus claws were hollow near their base, a feature that contributed to their poor preservation. Alxasaurus had enormous arms with long claws up to 40 cm, which it used to pull branches into its mouth.
The largest known Alxasaurus specimen was about 4 meters long and 3 meters tall.
This dinosaur had enormous arms with long claws up to 40 cm, which it used to pull branches into its mouth.
Alxasaurus possessed a semilunate carpal bone in its wrist, a feature found only in maniraptoran theropods like birds, dromaeosaurs, and troodontids.
Alxasaurus was discovered in 1988 during the China-Canada Dinosaur Project in the Bayin-Gobi Formation. Five Alxasaurus skeletons were recovered from the Bayin Gobi Formation in Inner Mongolia.

The genus Alxasaurus was formally described and named in 1993 by paleontologists Dong Zhiming and Dale Russell. Alxasaurus was described and named by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming and Canadian colleague Dale Russell in a 1993 publication.

The genus name Alxasaurus refers to the Alxa Desert in Inner Mongolia and the Greek word for lizard. The species name elesitaiensis honors the village of Elesitai near the fossil discovery site. The name Alxasaurus is derived from the Alxa Desert in Inner Mongolia, China, combined with the Greek word sauros meaning "lizard". The species name elesitaiensis honors the village of Elesitai, near where the fossils were found.

Alxasaurus likely had a beak and a large gut, adaptations suited for a herbivorous diet. Alxasaurus was a bipedal herbivore with a large abdomen to house a complex digestive system for processing vegetation.
Due to its phylogenetic position, it is possible that Alxasaurus had feathers.
Alxasaurus is classified within the family Alxasauridae. The family Alxasauridae was created to include Alxasaurus but is considered of dubious utility because it contains only a single species.
Alxasaurus belongs to the suborder Therizinosauria. Alxasaurus is a member of the order Saurischia. Alxasaurus is classified under the suborder Theropoda.
The only known species of Alxasaurus is A. elesitaiensis.

Alxasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) in Inner Mongolia. Alxasaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 100 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now Asia. The fossils date to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 to 100 million years ago.

The discovery of Alxasaurus supported the hypothesis that therizinosaurs were highly derived coelurosaurs rather than basal sauropodomorphs. While Alxasaurus exhibits typical therizinosaur features like body shape and teeth, its skeleton also demonstrates features present in more typical theropods.
